rationale: One bounded counterexample-backed proposal from hetzner-maker-request-v3.json only. Parent and oracle solve2/12. The noisy two-color demonstrations require painting every cell of complete empty3x3 patches color1 while preserving surrounding pixels. Existing one-pass local single-pixel painters cannot emit all nine cells from a center detection. Author a narrow typed repair of existing expert2, preserving its original convolution parameters and behavior outside an input-derived guard. The added branch detects all-zero3x3 input windows and emits their3x3 footprints. No seventh expert, task-ID dispatch, query-target inference, report-based tuning, or guaranteed gain is introduced. All newly added coefficients are literal authored values; existing Claude/GPT parent material remains inherited. This is branch assembly and structural repair, not crossover.
inheritance: Every existing tensor and five other expert structures are preserved exactly from the334-position parent in the authorized maker request. Expert2 retains its inherited convolution branch. The six-expert router stays exactly inherited, with no new dimensions or biases. Only the32 patch-branch scalar positions are newly authored.

executable_contract.guard: Let C be the set of distinct nonzero input colors. Enter the new branch iff0 occurs, C has exactly one member k, k is not1, and the number of nonzero input cells divided by total cells is strictly greater than patch.guard.density[0]. Otherwise run the original inherited expert2 convolution implementation exactly. This guard uses only input-derived palette and density, never task identity or expected outputs.
executable_contract.detect: Snapshot input. For each coordinate with a complete in-bounds3x3 window, sum patch.zero.W[0,inputcolor] across all nine input cells and add patch.detect.b[0]. Mark an anchor iff this is strictly positive. With the literal values, precisely nine zero cells are required. Coordinates whose3x3 window crosses the border are never anchors; absent pixels do not count as zero. Compute every anchor from original input, never generated output.
executable_contract.emit: For each output coordinate(r,c), sum patch.emit.W[dr+1,dc+1]*anchor[r-dr,c-dc] over dr,dc in{-1,0,1}, omitting invalid anchor coordinates, then add patch.emit.b[0]. If strictly positive, write argmax(patch.paint) with smallest-color tie-breaking; otherwise copy the original input pixel. This paints the union of detected3x3 footprints color1 and preserves all other input pixels.
executable_contract.router: Keep six experts and the inherited literal six-by-six identity router and zero bias. Recompute existing negative mean permitted-demonstration mismatch features using the actual repaired expert2 outputs. Preserve shape-mismatch penalty1 and existing tie-breaking. No expected query grid or task ID enters inference.
executable_contract.metric: Use unchanged exact whole-grid task correctness including dimensions. Fractional demo mismatch remains only an inference feature. Do not replace task success with pixel-level improvement.

assembly_decision: One charged candidate requires explicit translation/admission of guarded_conv_patch_emit_v1 at existing expert2. Preserve all old tensors, retain inherited convolution fallback, and freeze guard/detection/emission semantics before evaluation. This is a numerical branch proposal plus narrowly typed structural repair, not an already executed gain or automatic promotion. No seventh expert or router resize. Author effort is separately recorded from evaluation calls.
observed_limits: The dense two-color guard and3x3 patch hypothesis are inferred from permitted development examples. Larger empty regions emit the union of all qualifying3x3 windows; whether that generalizes is unverified.

Inside the new guard, inherited convolution behavior is replaced by patch emission; outside it the original family is preserved exactly. Existing other expert families and router coefficients are untouched.
Sparse marker drawing, reflected-object completion, row-color propagation, component filtering, panel movement, and shape-changing extraction failures remain unresolved by this branch.
The failure request contains duplicate cases for one task; no duplicates were treated as independent evidence or a gain.
No evaluation or reporting access was performed. Optional prior-child serialization is deferred; this file is the primary bounded proposal.
